# Why does direct buildModel(filename, model) result in TALOS without base pose, and how to explicitly add FreeFlyer?

> **Current answer:** Project contributors note that the floating base is not included in the standard URDF. Directly calling buildModel(filename, model) will fix the base to the universe, and q does not contain base position/orientation. When a humanoid has a floating base, a JointModelFreeFlyer root_joint should be constructed and a buildModel with root_joint called to override. The original author modified this and obtained TALOS model.nq=39, model.nv=38; compared to fixed base, 32/32, the configuration increased by 7 and speed increased by 6.

## Key terms

- Free-Flyer base (自由浮动基)
- Fixed base (固定基)
- Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) (机器人描述格式)
- Generalized configuration (广义配置)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why does Pinocchio's model.nq differ from model.nv, and why does HRP2 show nq=60, nv=30?
- Why does a model built directly from a humanoid URDF lack base position/orientation degrees of freedom?
- After importing HRP2, model.nq=60, model.nv=30; configuration dimension seems double the speed dimension.
- TALOS direct buildModel results in model.nq=model.nv=32, without expected 7/6 base degrees of freedom.

## Environment

- 2019 Pinocchio C++/Python; HRP2, ATLAS, TALOS URDF; specific software versions not mentioned.

## Priority diagnostics

- Check spherical, FreeFlyer, and continuous joint parameterizations; do not directly use nq as physical degrees of freedom.
- Check if buildModel explicitly passes JointModelFreeFlyer root_joint.

## Possible causes

- Quaternions are represented with 4 configuration components for 3 angular velocity dimensions, and continuous joints also use different manifold parameterizations for nq and nv.
- URDFs do not include floating base joints; direct buildModel fixes the base to the universe.

## Attempts

- Author changed joint type from continuous to revolute and rechecked nq/nv.
- Author followed the recommendation and called buildModel with JointModelFreeFlyer root_joint to re-import TALOS.

## Effective fixes

- Use randomConfiguration, integrate, and difference/differentiate for configuration, integration, and differentiation, without direct q += v or q1 - q0.
- Explicitly call buildModel with JointModelFreeFlyer root_joint when a floating base is present.

## Result

- Author reported HRP2's nq/nv match expectations after changing joint type from continuous to revolute.
- Author added FreeFlyer and obtained TALOS model.nq=39, model.nv=38, matching the maintainer's expectation.

## Limitations

- continuous and revolute have different angle boundary semantics; do not blindly replace them just to match dimensions in the model.
- q[0:3] and q[3:7] base translation/quaternion arrangements are only applicable to models with explicitly added FreeFlyer.
- Threaded based on 2019 interface; function names and overloads should be verified separately.
